The integration has been rewritten. the old configuration will not work. You will need to add the twitch integration via the new method.

## Proposed change
<!--

  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->
Converts old Twitch component to integration with config flow.

This is the first step. The next step is to split some attributes into new entities and add more data from the Twitch API.

Package change:
https://github.com/Teekeks/pyTwitchAPI/compare/v2.5.2...v2.5.7
https://github.com/Teekeks/pyTwitchAPI/releases

I don't know if there is a way of converting a sensor platform to a config flow so I will add this as a breaking change.

Original config:
```yaml
sensor:
  - platform: twitch
    client_id: !secret twitch_client_id
    client_secret: !secret twitch_client_secret
    channels:
      - twitchpresents
```

issue_context.title: Twitch entity_picture is incorrect when the streamer is live
issue_context.body:
### The problem

When a Twitch streamer is live (entity status is streaming) the entity_picture attribute is invalid - there appears to be a width and height parameters which aren't being filled out. For example in the developer tools under state I see:

entity_picture: https://static-cdn.jtvnw.net/previews-ttv/live_user_STREAMERNAME-{width}x{height}.jpg

As a result the entity picture in the UI is missing when the streamer is live.

If I visit that url in my browser and substitute a resolution such as 640x480 it pulls up a preview of the stream scaled to that size.

When the streamer is offline the entity_picture is appropriately set to their channel icon and appears correctly.



### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

core-2022.3.5

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

_No response_

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant OS

### Integration causing the issue

Twitch

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/twitch/

### Diagnostics information

_No response_

### Example YAML snippet

_No response_

### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

```txt
Nothing relevant in the logs.
```


### Additional information

I have not used the twitch integration before 2022.3.5.
comments:
I just updated Home Assistant from 2022.2.8 to 2022.3.8. The Twitch integration had been broken for me for quite some time so I had been making use of a custom component as a workaround. While updating HA, I removed that custom component and switched back to the built-in integration. This is what I see now:

![afbeelding](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/20402931/161361677-425885ef-cc86-407e-9066-5ad69f8d8b0b.png)

For now, I've resorted to downloading the pictures off of Twitch and customizing the affected entities. This is what it should look like (and what it previously looked like with the custom component):

![afbeelding](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/20402931/161361907-4db04e00-221c-45fc-8e2f-8e1a68de22ee.png)

Issue still exists.

Whenever a channel is not live, it shows a Twitch icon, whenever a channel is live, it shows nothing because it's looking for this entity picture:
https://static-cdn.jtvnw.net/previews-ttv/live_user_CHANNELNAME-{width}x{height}.jpg

Whenever the resolution is hardcoded in the url, it does work

Please make sure to update to the latest Home Assistant version and check if that solves the issue. Let us know if that works for you by adding a comment 👍
This issue has now been marked as stale and will be closed if no further activity occurs. Thank you for your contributions.

As far as I can tell, this issue still exists, at least on 2022.8.5.
I have not yet updated to 2022.9.x but the release notes don't seem to contain any changes for the Twitch component.
